svg.title: The “Final Solution”: Rail Deportations, Extermination Camps & Resistance (1942–44)
svg.desc: KS3 Year 9 historical GIS atlas map of Axis-dominated Europe (1942–1944) showing the Wannsee Villa in Berlin (20 January 1942), continental railway deportation vectors from France, the Netherlands, Italy, Greece, and Hungary to Occupied Poland, Operation Reinhard death camps (Bełżec, Sobibór, Treblinka), Auschwitz-Birkenau, the April–May 1943 Warsaw Ghetto Uprising and camp revolts, and the October 1943 Danish sea rescue of ~7,200 Jews to Neutral Sweden.

svg.text: KS3 HISTORY • YEAR 9 ENQUIRY: THE SHOAH
The “Final Solution”: Rail Deportations, Death Camps & Resistance (1942–44)
After Wannsee (Jan 1942), Nazi ministries & railways deported Jews across Europe to six extermination camps in Occupied Poland.
Yet Jewish fighters rose up in Warsaw, Treblinka, Sobibór & Birkenau—and Denmark proved neighbours could rescue ~7,200 lives.
